questions.question: The complex number \(z = x + jy\) which satisfy the equation \(|z + 1| = 1\) lie on
options: a circle with \((1, 0)\) as the centre and radius \(1\)
a circle with \((-1, 0)\) as the centre and radius \(1\)
questions.explanation: Given the equation: \[|z + 1| = 1\] If \(z = x + jy\)\[|x + jy + 1| = 1\] \[|(x + 1) + jy| = 1\] Taking the magnitude on both sides: \[\sqrt{(x + 1)^2 + y^2} = 1\] Squaring both sides: \[(x + 1)^2 + y^2 = 1^2\] This is the standard equation of a circle: \[(x - x_0)^2 + (y - y_0)^2 = R^2\] Comparing the terms, we get centre: \((x_0, y_0) = (-1, 0)\) and radius: \(R = 1\). \[\boxed{\text{B.a circle with $(-1, 0)$ as the centre and radius $1$}}\]

questions.question: The operational amplifier use a differential input stage with a constant current source mainly to obtain
questions.explanation: A differential amplifier uses a constant current source (tail current source) to keep the total emitter current nearly constant. This greatly reduces the effect of common-mode input signals, thereby improving the Common Mode Rejection Ratio (CMRR). \[A_{CM}\approx 0\] Hence, the common-mode gain becomes very small while the differential gain remains high. \[\boxed{\text{(a) Very low common mode gain}}\]

questions.subject: analog-electronics
questions.question: A common emitter transistor amplifier using a collector load of \(1~\text{k}\Omega\) and operating at room temperature with \(I_C=1~\text{mA}\), gives a voltage gain of nearly equal to
questions.explanation:
For a common emitter amplifier, the small-signal voltage gain is approximately \[A_{v}=g_{m}R_{C}\] where \[g_{m}=\frac{I_{C}}{V_{T}}\] At room temperature, \[V_{T}\approx25\,\text{mV}\] Hence, \[g_{m}=\frac{1\,\text{mA}}{25\,\text{mV}}
=0.04\,\text{S}\] Therefore, \[A_{v}=0.04\times1000=40\] \[\boxed{\textbf{(b) }40}\]

questions.subject: digital-electronics
questions.question: A 4-bit synchronous counter with a series carry, uses flipflop and AND gates, having a propagation delay of 30 ns and 10 ns respectively. The maximum time interval required between two successive clock pulses for reliable operation of the counter is
questions.explanation:
Given:
  • 4-bit synchronous counter with a series carry using flipflop and AND gate
  • Propagation delays of flipflop and AND gate are 30 ns and 10 ns respectively
Frequency of operation of synchronous counter is given by: \[f \le \frac{1}{30 \text{ ns} + 10 \text{ ns}}\] So the time period between successful clock pulses \(T = \dfrac{1}{f} = ]\dfrac{1}{40 \text{ ns} } = 40 \text{ ns}\) \[\boxed{(C) \; 40 \text{ ns}}\]

questions.subject: digital-electronics
questions.question: A sample-and-hold circuit is normally required before the following type of A/D converter
questions.explanation: Among different types of ADCs, the successive approximation type ADC requires a Sample-and-Hold (S/H) circuit at its front end. This is necessary because the successive approximation algorithm evaluates the input signal bit by bit over multiple clock cycles, comparing the input against a sequence of reference voltages generated by an internal DAC. If the input signal changes during this multi-cycle evaluation, the comparison results would be inconsistent, leading to an incorrect digital output. Therefore, an S/H circuit is astutely critical for a successive approximation quantizer in order to keep the input waveform stable during the successive iterations of bit evaluation. \[\boxed{(A) \text{ Successive approximation}}\]

options: the address of the next operand
the current size of the stack
the address of the top of the stack
the address for storing the result of arithmetic operations
questions.explanation: The stack pointer in a microprocessor is a register containing the address of the top of the stack and it works on last in first out principle. \[\boxed{(C) \text{ the address of the top of the stack}}\]

questions.subject: control-systems
questions.question: The transfer function of a control system is given by: \(\dfrac{C(s)}{R(s)} = \dfrac{25}{s^2 + 6s + 25}\). The first maximum value of the response occurs at a time \(t_{\max}\) given by
questions.explanation:
Given transfer function: \[\frac{C(s)}{R(s)} = \frac{25}{s^2 + 6s + 25}\] Comparing the denominator with \(s^2 + 2\zeta\omega_n s + \omega_n^2\): \[\begin{aligned} \omega_n^2 = 25 &\implies \omega_n = 5\,\text{rad/s} \\ 2\zeta\omega_n = 6 &\implies 2\zeta(5) = 6 \implies \zeta = 0.6 \end{aligned}\] The first maximum value of the step response occurs at the peak time \(t_p\) (where \(n = 1\)): \[t_{\max} = t_p = \frac{\pi}{\omega_n\sqrt{1 - \zeta^2}}\] \[t_{\max} = \frac{\pi}{5\sqrt{1 - (0.6)^2}} = \frac{\pi}{5 \times 0.8} = \frac{\pi}{4}\] \[\boxed{(B) \ \ \dfrac{\pi}{4}}\]
Key points
  • Peak time formula: \(t_p = \dfrac{n\pi}{\omega_d} = \dfrac{n\pi}{\omega_n\sqrt{1 - \zeta^2}}\).
  • Overshoot maxima occur at odd values of \(n\) (\(n = 1, 3, 5, \dots\)), whereas undershoot minima occur at even values of \(n\) (\(n = 2, 4, 6, \dots\)).

questions.question: The transfer function of a basic PD controller is given by (\(K\)'s are real constants)
questions.explanation:
A basic proportional-derivative (PD) controller consists of proportional and derivative actions only. Hence, its transfer function is: \[G_c(s)=K_p+K_ds\] Comparing with the given options, \(K_p=K_0\) and \(K_d=K_2\), \[G_c(s)=K_0+K_2s\] \[\boxed{(B)\;K_0+K_2s}\]
Key points
  • A P controller: \(K_p\)
  • A PI controller: \(K_p+\dfrac{K_i}{s}\)
  • A PD controller: \(K_p+K_ds\)
  • A PID controller: \(K_p+\dfrac{K_i}{s}+K_ds\)
